summary: This bill makes it a federal crime (with up to 10 years in prison) to perform surgeries, hormone treatments, or puberty blockers on anyone under 18 to address gender dysphoria except for specific disorders of sex development, bars Medicare coverage and provider participation for such treatments, and prohibits any federal funding for them.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits federal funding (including Medicare payments and any other appropriated funds) for gender-related medical treatments on minors. This directly reduces government expenditures in this narrow area, though the overall fiscal impact is small.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill restricts specific medical procedures under Medicare and federal programs but does not alter the overall structure of public vs. private healthcare delivery or coverage systems.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill addresses medical treatments related to gender transition for minors but makes no reference to abortion access or restrictions.
No provisions affect military or defense spending.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill excludes certain treatments from Medicare coverage, which is a minor scaling back of benefits within a safety-net program, but the effect is narrowly targeted.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug decriminalization, enforcement, or controlled substances policy.

The bill creates a new federal criminal offense with penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment for performing prohibited treatments on minors, representing an expansion of criminal enforcement in this area.
No provisions relate to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
By prohibiting certain federal expenditures, the bill has a very minor effect of prioritizing reduced spending over deficit acceptance.

The core purpose of the bill is to criminalize and defund gender-affirming medical treatments for minors, directly limiting access to care for transgender youth and thereby restricting legal protections and medical options for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or online platforms.
No provisions address labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
The bill imposes a blanket prohibition without referencing religious exemptions or balancing against anti-discrimination protections.

Section 4 explicitly bars all federal funds and trust-fund monies from being used for gender-related medical treatments on minors, and sections 3(a)–(b) exclude such treatments from Medicare coverage and bar participating providers. These provisions reduce federal outlays, producing a modest deficit-reducing effect, but the fiscal language is incidental to the bill’s core purpose of criminal prohibition.

The Medicare exclusions and broad federal-funding ban in sections 3 and 4 remove government payment and provider participation for the specified treatments, thereby decreasing federal involvement in this narrow slice of healthcare. The changes are secondary to the primary criminal prohibition and do not address market competition or cost-reduction mechanisms more generally.
